title: Lakshya Sen beats Koki Watanabe to win Kumamoto Masters, his second title in a row
dek: The world No. 13 lost the first game before winning 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in 64 minutes. He is the first Indian to win the tournament, and the win lifts his hopes of reaching the World Tour Finals.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Lakshya Sen won the Kumamoto Masters Japan, a BWF Super 500 tournament, on Sunday, coming from a game down to beat Japan's Koki Watanabe 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 in one hour and four minutes. It was his second title in successive tournaments, after the Hylo Open in Germany earlier this month, and he is the first Indian to win the men's singles at the event, first held in 2023, according to reports.

Watanabe, playing at home, took the first game comfortably. Sen, the world No. 13 and eighth seed, edged the second 21-18 and led the decider 11-7 at the interval before closing it out. He had lost both his earlier meetings with Watanabe this year. Watanabe had knocked out India's Kidambi Srikanth in the quarter-finals.

On Saturday Sen beat Indonesia's Alwi Farhan, the world No. 10, 21-12, 15-21, 21-11 in the semi-finals, his first win over him in three matches.

The two titles have lifted Sen eight places to 10th in the race for the BWF World Tour Finals, close to the cut-off for the eight qualifiers, according to reports. The Finals are due in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December.
